title: The More AI Reshapes B2B, The More Human It Needs To Become
summary: Explore how AI in B2B marketing makes brand preference, human judgment, and trust more valuable — and why marketing must become connected.
body_markdown:
Earlier this month, we had the pleasure of attending and presenting Forrester predictions at The Drum’s


[B2B World Fest 2026](https://www.b2bworldfest.com/event/a3897d6f-3048-4c38-ae3f-6165880eff49/home) event in Miami. AI dominated the conversation, of course, but what stood out was the tension underneath it. B2B marketers are moving quickly toward an AI-mediated world, but the things that create preference, trust, and confidence are becoming more important. The event itself reflected a B2B industry increasingly focused on earning attention through better work and bigger stories.


Here are the four themes we took away.


1.


### **Brand matters** **more** **when buyers have more choices.**


One of the clearest messages was the renewed importance of brand and


[preference marketing](https://www.forrester.com/report/pivot-from-pointless-pipeline-pursuit-to-preference-marketing/RES192854) . AI is making it dramatically easier for buyers to research providers, compare offerings, and assemble shortlists. But easier comparison makes preference more valuable.


According to


[Forrester’s Business Buyers’ Insights Survey, 2026](https://www.forrester.com/data-and-insights/surveys/forresters-business-buyers-insights-survey-2026/SUS200000240) , at the very beginning of the purchase process, 74% of buyers already have a front-runner in mind, and 60% of the time, that preferred vendor wins. Thought leadership delivered through an expanded


[buying network](https://www.forrester.com/report/buying-networks-your-buyers-new-reality/RES182145) helps companies move beyond awareness to become considered, trusted, and ultimately chosen. That matters in an AI-mediated buying environment. An AI agent may identify the provider that meets a written specification or offers the lowest price, but B2B decisions involve more than specifications. Buyers bring existing technology investments, relationships, approved vendor lists, perceptions of support, and confidence in a provider’s longevity to the purchase table. Brand preference doesn’t disappear because an agent enters the process. Marketers will increasingly need to influence both the people setting the rules for AI agents and the agents themselves.


1.


### **Stop debating whether to use AI and start learning where it creates value.**


The conversation in Miami centered around how to apply AI intelligently. AI can help marketers generate and remake creative, test ideas rapidly, personalize content, optimize campaigns, and explore audiences using synthetic personas. But efficiency shouldn’t be confused with effectiveness. In our


[predictions](https://www.forrester.com/report/predictions-2027-b2b-go-to-market/RES202076) presentation, we warned that companies risk cutting marketing capacity based on AI productivity gains that don’t fully materialize. The better strategy is to use automation to augment people and redirect their time toward work that creates differentiated value.


The same principle applies to synthetic research and creative. Synthetic personas can make testing faster and more scalable, but they need foundations in primary research and proprietary knowledge, along with clear validation rules. AI accelerates the work. It shouldn’t become a substitute for understanding the customer.


1.


### **As AI becomes ubiquitous, human interaction becomes a differentiator.**


Perhaps the biggest paradox of the event was that the more AI enters B2B buying and selling, the more valuable human interaction becomes. Data supporting one of the Forrester predictions we shared was that 94% of business buyers report using or planning to use AI answer engines during the buying journey, yet only 13% trust AI-generated recommendations. One-third already turn to humans to validate outcomes through conversations with providers, analysts, customer references, and partners.


That’s why we


[predict](https://www.forrester.com/report/predictions-2027-business-buyers/RES202072) that buyers will double their human interactions to validate AI-generated recommendations. AI is exceptional at finding, synthesizing, and comparing information. But it can’t fully determine whether a provider is right for a buyer’s particular circumstances, nor can it assume accountability for a consequential decision.


### **Real-time problem solving is still a human skill. And AI doesn’t have accountability — humans do.**


This means companies shouldn’t automate away the very people that buyers will increasingly need: subject-matter experts, customer success leaders, sellers, partners, analysts, and customer advocates who can add context and build confidence.


1.


### **Marketing has to become a connected system.**


Another idea that resonated with us during the event was that


[planning](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-future-of-b2b-marketing-planning-is-intelligence-driven/RES180097) can no longer happen as a series of disconnected activities. Research informs segmentation. Segmentation informs opportunity selection and positioning. Positioning shapes objectives, product, pricing, distribution, production, and budget. Change one, and the others may need to change with it.


AI makes that interconnectedness even more important because it dramatically increases the speed at which organizations can act. The danger is accelerating one piece of the system without understanding its impact on everything else.


The takeaway from Miami wasn’t that AI replaces B2B marketing. It was almost the opposite:


### **AI is raising the value of what machines can’t commoditize: distinctive brands, original ideas, trusted evidence, creative thinking, human judgment, relationships, and accountability.**


The winners will be the ones that use AI to amplify value realization for buyers.
